extracted.intended_audience: Prospective offerors (academia, industry, research organizations, small businesses, international researchers) preparing white papers and full proposals to ONR / ONR Global / MCWL under BAA N0001425SB001
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of white papers and full proposals in response to ONR/ONRG/MCWL Long Range BAA N0001425SB001, including eligibility, required formats, content elements, registrations, classification and marking, and instrument-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAA scope and competitive procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: This publication constitutes a Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) for awards by ONR, ONR Global, and MCWL and constitutes a merit-based, competitive procedure in accordance with DoDGARS and FAR guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR may fund all, some, or none of the proposals received. A formal RFP/solicitation will not be issued. No reimbursement of proposal development costs. Proposals treated as sensitive competitive information and disclosed only for evaluation purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: BAA calls posting & submission window
rubrics_metrics.description: BAA Calls will be posted to the ONR website, SAM (sam.gov), and, if applicable, Grants.gov; this announcement remains open for approximately one year from publication and proposals may be submitted at any time during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government reserves the right not to review proposals submitted under this BAA after 30 September 2025 or after a successor BAA is issued, whichever occurs first. Interested parties should periodically check the listed websites for BAA Calls and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: All responsible sources from academia, industry and the research community worldwide may submit proposals; HBCUs and Minority Institutions are encouraged; both small and large businesses are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FFRDCs, DoE national labs, Navy laboratories, military universities, warfare centers, and other DoD/civilian agency laboratories are not eligible to receive awards (teaming with eligible principals may be allowed if permitted by sponsoring agreement). UARCs are eligible unless precluded by their DoD contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for competition (supplementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for supplementation of existing projects are eligible to compete with applications for new federal awards under this BAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should ensure disclosures of current and pending support are accurate—such disclosures may render an applicant ineligible and DoD may request updates throughout the period of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted fundamental research policy
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR follows the Under Secretary of Defense (AT&L) Memorandum definition of 'contracted fundamental research' and DoD policy regarding what constitutes fundamental vs non-fundamental research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental research includes research funded by RDT&E Budget Activity 1 (Basic Research) or Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) when performed on-campus at a university. Applied research performed off-campus or Budget Activity 3–4 activities are not contracted fundamental research and may require restrictions and DoD pre-publication review. Offerors should consult the appropriate ONR Technical POC to determine classification and, if subcontractors conduct fundamental research, prime must identify and confirm that work is fundamental research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing / matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing is not expected under contracts and assistance awards and will not be used as a factor during merit review; voluntary cost sharing may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional guidance available at 2 CFR 200.306 and FAR 35.003. OT-specific cost sharing information is in the OTA for Research section (10 U.S.C. § 4021 / § 4022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument types and their characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may take the form of procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, and Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for Research or Prototypes, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and implications: procurement contracts acquire property/services for government use; grants transfer value to carry out public purpose (no substantial government involvement); cooperative agreements anticipate substantial involvement; OTAs for Research may include a 50/50 cost share 'to the maximum extent practicable' and must not duplicate existing DoD programs; OTAs for Prototypes may allow follow-on production if conditions are met. Offerors should consult the referenced OTA guides (June/July 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model contracts and grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of model contracts and grants are provided on the ONR website for illustrative purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conflicts exist between examples and current FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses, the current FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses govern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal confidentiality and FOIA/OT exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain information submitted during the solicitation and award process of an OT or Cooperative Agreement are exempt from FOIA disclosure for five years under 10 U.S.C. §4021(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should mark documents with a legend asserting they are submitted on a confidential basis. Examples of exempt items: a proposal, proposal abstract, supporting documents; a business plan submitted on a proprietary basis; technical information submitted on a controlled basis (e.g., distribution statements per DoDI 5230.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking proprietary data and required legend
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must appropriately mark each page that contains proprietary information and may use a specific legend on the title page to assert restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample title-page legend text is provided in the BAA; each sheet to be restricted must also carry a second-sheet legend. The sample legend explains limited duplication/use by the Government for evaluation and rights if awarded a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-proprietary Statement of Work (SOW)
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must include a non-proprietary version of the Statement of Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include proprietary data or markings in the non-proprietary SOW. If classified proposals are submitted, an unclassified SOW must accompany them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal titles should be descriptive of the work and not merely a copy of the BAA announcement title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose titles that convey the essence of the proposed effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper format
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers should be formatted with 8.5 x 11-inch paper, 1-inch margins, single-spaced, Times New Roman 12 point, and are limited to 5 pages (excluding cover page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow exact formatting; cover page is excluded from page limit and is mandatory for ONR and ONRG submissions. FedConnect will not accept a white paper unless the Cover Page is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper required content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers shall include a mandatory cover page and substantive sections: Technical Concept; Future Naval Relevance; Operational Naval Concept (where applicable); Operational Utility Assessment Plan (where applicable); and a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page: Use ONR/ONRG cover page templates (links provided). For ONR/ONRG, Program Officer / Science Director information and correct email address are required fields on the cover page to ensure the submission is received by the correct official.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper file format for email submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When email submission is required, white paper files must be Microsoft Word 2016 or PDF compatible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to file compatibility to prevent rejection or unreadability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal format & appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals must conform to the instructions provided in the BAA appendices: Appendix 1 for Grants and Cooperative Agreements; Appendix 2 for Contracts and Other Transaction Agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instrument-specific instructions in the appendices for content, formatting, submission, and additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and entity identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All offerors must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), obtain a CAGE Code, and maintain active SAM registration while under consideration or holding an active Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply may render an applicant not qualified to receive a Federal award; SAM may be accessed at sam.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security classification and classified proposal submission
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers and Proposals are expected to be unclassified, but classified submissions are permitted; a non-classified SOW is required with any classified proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified proposals must be submitted to ONR’s Document Control Unit at the specified address with specified outer/inner envelope markings; do not email classified questions—follow the Security POC process to ask classified questions securely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications and question submission protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Unclassified communications should be submitted via e-mail to the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) with a copy to the Contract/Business POC and/or Grants POC. Do not submit questions via the FedConnect Message Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For classified questions, send an unclassified email to the ONR Security POC requesting to ask a classified question; the Security POC will arrange secure communication. Use the specific TPOCs listed for ONR, ONR Global, and MCWL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer information requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The ONR or ONRG Program Officer (or ONRG Science Director) information and correct email address are required on the cover page to ensure receipt by the Program Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program Officer information can be found on the ONR website (links provided) and is mandatory for FedConnect acceptance of white papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team cooperation and data exchange expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Teams are encouraged and may submit proposals, but offerors must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data and other information in an integrated program with other contractors and system integrators selected by ONR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate willingness to share information and integrate with other performers where required by the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of current and pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must disclose current and pending support; such disclosures may render an applicant ineligible for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD may request updated continuing and pending support information prior to award and throughout the period of performance; ensure accuracy and timeliness of updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: TINA / certified cost or pricing data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals meeting the Truth in Negotiations Act (TINA) threshold are subject to certified cost and pricing data requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors required to execute the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data as soon as practicable but no later than five business days after the date of price agreement. Cost/pricing data submitted after price agreement will be dispositioned post-award to determine if data up to price agreement was defective and whether a price adjustment is due (FAR 15.407-1, FAR 52.215-10/11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) disclosure & mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must disclose actual or potential Organizational Conflicts of Interest and provide a Mitigation Plan where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCI Mitigation Plans must describe actions to avoid or mitigate OCIs (including reassignment processes, NDAs, training, evidence of mitigation). The Contracting Officer will review certifications/statements and may require additional information; refusal to disclose required OCI information will disqualify the offeror. If mitigation is accepted, it becomes part of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations regarding covered telecommunications equipment (Section 889)
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must make representations about providing or using covered telecommunications equipment or services (per Section 889 prohibitions) and disclose detailed information if they respond affirmatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an offeror indicates it 'will' provide or 'does' use covered equipment/services, they must disclose manufacturer, entity name, UEI/CAGE, model numbers, descriptions, and explanation of proposed use or permissibility. Offerors should review excluded parties in SAM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced cybersecurity controls for CUI
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain performers may be required to implement enhanced cyber security controls to protect controlled unclassified information (CUI) on unclassified networks if the Chief of Naval Research determines such controls are warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These controls are in addition to DFARS clause 252.204-7012 requirements. Offerors are strongly encouraged to consult the cognizant Program Officer to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on production authority for prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract issued under this BAA may be awarded or later modified to contain a contract line item or option for development/demonstration or initial production of technology developed under the contract in accordance with 10 U.S.C. 4004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority applies where components/items were created as a result of work performed under the contract; OTAs may also permit follow-on production under specified conditions (10 U.S.C. § 4022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with applicable FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with applicable FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses and may be required to include listed provisions/clauses and certifications in proposals and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BAA lists example clauses that may be applicable (e.g., system for award management, anti-kickback, safeguarding covered defense information, limitations on telecom equipment, patent reporting, etc.). ONR reserves the right to include relevant/current clauses necessary based on award dollar value; offerors should review and understand referenced clauses and be prepared to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: FedConnect / submission platform requirements (cover page & FedConnect acceptance)
rubrics_metrics.description: FedConnect will not accept a white paper unless the prescribed cover page is included; white paper submission portals have specific required components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ONR/ONRG cover page templates/links. Ensure Program Officer info is correct on the cover page for ONR/ONRG submissions to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper page limit and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers are limited to 5 pages excluding the cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to the page limit; formatting requirements (font, margins, spacing) must be followed or risk rejection.
